clusters.state_of_play: Houthis have rapidly seized Yemen's Red Sea coast and captured two strategic Red Sea islands, disrupting shipping and triggering a humanitarian crisis with over 100,000 Yemenis displaced (UN) amid renewed fighting; Qatar warns of catastrophe if Houthis seize full control of the Bab al-Mandab strait. A Houthi drone was intercepted near Mecca, prompting Saudi Arabia to declare pilgrim security a 'red line' as the Houthis denied targeting the holy city and the OIC condemned the attack; Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree further claimed the group downed a Saudi fighter jet as the war intensifies. Iran's planned security talks with Iraq and Gulf states in Oman remain postponed amid lack of consensus over Hormuz shipping, even as a vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz, explosions were reported on Iran's Qeshm island near the strait, and a drone attack (blamed by Saudi Arabia on Iranian-backed Iraqi militias) shut down Saudi Arabia's major East-West pipeline, now estimated to threaten up to 5% of global oil supply, pushing oil above $108/barrel and diesel to record highs, spiking US Treasury yields to 5% amid a bond sell-off, and dragging down Wall Street and other global stock markets including Australia's ASX. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met a U.S. commander seeking more military support but faces a 'strategic shock' after apparent U.S. rebuffs, amid stalled U.S.-Iran diplomacy, Trump floating US retention of seized Iranian oil akin to Venezuela, and a widening Mideast conflict. Separately, Germany's far-right AfD scored major gains in state elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, delivering the CDU its worst result since 1949 and pushing Die Linke ahead in Berlin; Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the outcome a 'disaster' but vowed to remain in office and press ahead with reforms, even as AfD leader Alice Weidel demanded he step down and analysts noted AfD still lacks coalition partners to form a government.
